questions.cardText:
[Art History] Which of the following best describes how a traditional Chinese landscape painting might differ from a Western painting?
A. It places the vanishing point outside of the painting to create depth
B. It does not use any perspective
C. It uses multiple perspectives within a single composition
Answer: C. Many traditional Chinese paintings, particularly of the Northern Song dynasty, combine different parts of a landscape seen from various angles within a single composition. This approach creates a more dynamic and immersive experience, in contrast to the single-point perspective often used in Western art.
questions.de: Wie nennt man den Blickpunkt der traditionellen chinesischen Landschaftsmalerei, der sich innerhalb eines Bildes auf und ab sowie nah und fern bewegt, statt der westlichen festen Zentralperspektive?
questions.en: What is the name for the viewpoint of traditional Chinese landscape painting that moves up and down and near and far within one picture, instead of the Western single fixed perspective?

timeline.labelEn: Song dynasty, the classic age of Chinese landscape painting
timeline.labelDe: Song-Dynastie, das klassische Zeitalter der chinesischen Landschaftsmalerei

source.title: Chinese Landscape Painting during the Song Dynasty

questions.notes: Card correct. The Princeton University Art Museum page calls it “shifting perspective”; other names are “floating” or “moving” perspective (散点透视), and Guo Xi’s “three distances” theory is related — accept these.

questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] How many teeth does a typical adult human have?
A. 28 B. 32 C. 36
Answer: B.
questions.de: Wie viele bleibende Zähne hat ein erwachsener Mensch normalerweise, Weisheitszähne eingeschlossen?
questions.en: How many permanent teeth does a typical adult human have, wisdom teeth included?

timeline.labelEn: Bartolomeo Eustachi publishes his study of the structure of the teeth
timeline.labelDe: Bartolomeo Eustachi veröffentlicht seine Studie über den Bau der Zähne

questions.notes: Card correct: 32 permanent teeth (16 upper, 16 lower), 20 primary. Many adults have fewer because wisdom teeth are missing or removed — hence “wisdom teeth included”. Timeline from Wikipedia’s Bartolomeo Eustachi page (works on the teeth, 1562–63).
